clips.title: Why AI Coding Agents Get Stuck in Infinite Loops (And How to Fix It)
clips.why: The loop patterns that agents fall into, taken from a review of thousands of agent runs.
look: Which patterns match our four: the same command, the same error, undo and redo, ping-pong.
Ask yourself which of these patterns would make an agent look busy from the outside.
clips.after: Our watcher gives each of these patterns a name, and the name goes into the first nudge the agent reads.

clips.title: Your AI agent is stuck in a loop. Here is how Gemini CLI catches it | Agent Internals
clips.why: A tour of the loop detection in Gemini CLI, Google's open-source coding agent: fingerprint every tool call, look for a repeating pattern, then react.
look: How a tool call becomes a fingerprint, like our normalized input and output hashes.
How a repeating pattern is found in the recent calls.
What Gemini CLI does when it finds one: warn once, then stop. Compare it with our ladder, which never stops a run.
clips.after: We detect loops the same way, but we answer with five cheap rungs instead of a stop, because in our platform only a person ends a run that is still working.

clips.title: Claude Code Effort vs Thinking: What's the Difference?
clips.channel: Stefan Wirth - AI without the BS
clips.why: Changing the effort level has a cost: it can make the prompt cache cold, which is why we change it only at step boundaries and only for the step that failed.
look: What happens to the cache when effort changes.
Why that matters for a long session.
clips.after: The third rung re-runs one step one level higher in the same session, and the first spike checks that cache reads stay high when we do it.

practice.q: Which of these tool events counts as real progress for the watcher?

options.text: npm test -- ProjectsTable passes, after it failed twice
options.why: A check that failed before and now passes is the clearest progress there is.
Running the test is activity. A failure that was already known teaches nothing new.
An edit may be useful, but it only proves something when a check passes afterwards.
Only the first read of a file is a new fact.

practice.q: Errors are compared by their signature. Fill in what the signature masks, so that "Timeout of 5002 ms" and "Timeout of 5004 ms" match.
practice.hint: One letter that stands for any number.
practice.why: Numbers such as times, ports and line counts change between attempts of the same error, so they are masked before comparing.

practice.q: Progress stays flat. Put the rungs of the ladder in order.
items: Nudge: name the loop and ask for a different approach
Re-plan: write a short new plan for this step
Think harder: re-run the step one effort level higher
Fresh start: checkpoint, then a new session seeded with notes.md
Ask a person in the ticket's thread, with the evidence
practice.why: Each rung costs a little more than the one before, and a person's attention is the most expensive, so it comes last.

practice.q: Why does the fresh start wait for a step boundary instead of happening the moment the counter reaches 15?

options.text: It needs a checkpoint first, and ending a session in the middle of a turn would throw away the work of that turn
options.why: Between turns, after a checkpoint, the new session starts from saved work and notes.md, so only the cluttered context is lost.

options.text: The Agent SDK cannot end a session during a turn
options.why: A session can be interrupted. We choose not to, because of the work in flight.

options.text: The ladder can only count at step boundaries
options.why: The watcher counts every tool event, and the first two rungs happen inside the turn.

practice.q: A build step's checks fail with Opus 5.5 at medium effort. What does the routing rule do?

options.text: Re-run that step once at high, in the same session
options.why: One level up, once, with applyFlagSettings at the step boundary, so the prompt cache stays warm. After that, the watcher and its ladder handle the step.

options.text: Re-run the whole ticket at xhigh
options.why: Only the failed step goes up, and only one level. Everything else stays at medium.

options.text: Switch to a new session with a bigger model
options.why: A new session would lose the warm cache and the context. The rule keeps the session and changes only the effort.
